source.title: Predictive Scaling Laws for Efficient GRPO Training of Large Reasoning Models
source.authors: Datta Nimmaturi; Vaishnavi Bhargava; Rajat Ghosh; Johnu George; Debojyoti Dutta

record.tranche_reason: The study reports reward dynamics during GRPO fine-tuning, not held-out pretraining cross-entropy scaling, small-run extrapolation, compute-optimal allocation, or the other specified versions. Its findings are related but measure a different outcome.
record.gate_note: The study measures evaluation reward during GRPO fine-tuning and reports final reward by model. It does not report held-out pretraining loss, scaling with training tokens or compute, or a fixed-compute allocation. The GRPO reward results are recorded as findings about a related but different measure; cited results from other work are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study fits curves to GRPO evaluation reward against normalized training step during LoRA fine-tuning of four quantized instruct models. It reports no held-out loss and no scaling of loss with parameters, data or compute. Model size enters its fit as a linear term estimated from only two sizes per family. The 'scaling law' it names is a within-run learning-curve fit for a different construct, so it bears on no version. V5 (fine-tuning regime) and V6 (downstream improving with scale) are the nearest, but neither is tested: the measure is training-time reward, not loss scaling or downstream performance across a range of scales.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that GRPO reward curves follow a consistent three-phase, saturation-shaped trajectory across all four models, and that a parametric law conditioned on model size, initial reward and normalized progress predicts the plateau. They also conclude that training beyond about 20% of normalized steps (roughly the last 80% of one epoch) adds negligible reward, so early stopping can cut GRPO compute. They further state that parameter count dominates final reward, more than architecture family.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses quantized instruct models, LoRA, GRPO, and evaluation reward during post-training; it does not reproduce the original pretraining-loss scaling measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcomes differ across model sizes; reward trajectory phases are described as similar across the tested model families and sizes.

fits_no_version.finding: Final GRPO reward is about 2.4x higher for the 7–8B models than for the 3B models in each family (Llama 20.8 vs 8.7; Qwen 19.8 vs 8.4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within these GRPO LoRA runs, larger checkpoints reach higher final evaluation reward than smaller ones in the same family.

fits_no_version.finding: Reward trajectories show slow, rapid and plateau phases at about 0.1 and 0.2 normalized steps. The authors fit a sigmoid with a linear model-size term (beta=2.5, delta=39.9, t0=0.1). They also state a power law in training steps (Eq. 4, alpha≈0.3) without fit statistics.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: GRPO evaluation reward over training steps follows a saturating (sigmoid or power-law) curve, with the plateau starting around 20% of one epoch.

record.problems: Only four quantized instruct models, one dataset, and one stated training setup are tested. The reported curves do not provide uncertainty estimates, and the study's reward metric and post-training setting do not establish held-out pretraining-loss scaling.

untested.parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or compute.
Extrapolation from small to much larger runs.
Effect of depth, width or other shape choices on loss at a fixed parameter count.
Power-law loss scaling with model or data size in a fine-tuning or RL regime. Only within-run reward curves are fitted.
Predictable downstream gains over a range of scales. There are only two sizes per family and no held-out benchmark trend.
Dependence of published exponents or allocations on fitting or setup choices.

missing.what: The fitted parameters of the sigmoid reward law (alpha=1.009, beta=2.500, gamma=0.401, delta=39.875, t0=0.1) and the Eq. 4 step power law (alpha≈0.3). Neither is in the rows. They bear on no version and would belong under fits_no_version.
missing.locator: Theoritical Reward Scaling Law; Results and Analysis (fitted global parameters)

record.verdict_notes: The record's relation (discusses) and tranche (T6) are kept. The paper uses scaling-law language but measures within-run RL reward, with no uncertainty, one dataset and four models. Its curve-fit claims are weak: there are no goodness-of-fit numbers, and the text calls the same curves both power-law and sigmoid. All rows correctly carry ['none'].

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute.
Whether fits from small pretraining runs predict much larger runs.
The loss-minimising parameter and token allocation at fixed compute.
Architecture effects on held-out pretraining loss at fixed parameter count.
Whether the same power-law form for held-out loss holds in other modalities or training regimes.
Predictability of downstream performance from scale or pretraining loss.
Dependence of the original laws or their fitted exponents and compute-optimal split on setup and fitting choices.
